newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak parliament approves new bank privatisation law.
newsitem.headline: Slovak parliament approves new bank privatisation law.

text.p: Slovak parliament on Wednesday approved a new privatisation law effectively allowing the selloff of state stakes in two major banks, but only after a last minute concession by opposition deputies.

Parliament approved the measure, which replaced a draft halting the sale of four financial institutions until 2003, after the opposition accepted a government plan to leave the two largest -- insurer Slovenska Poistovna and savings bank Slovenska Sporitelna -- untouched.
The measure thus allows two other major commerical banks, IRB and VUB, to be privatised.
"We gave political guarantees to the ZRS (Workers' Party) that Sporitelna and Poistovna will not be privatised until the end of this term," Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik told parliament.
The law was then approved by a large majority, with 124 of the deputies present voting in favour, three against, and 12 abstentions. Four deputies did not vote at all.

Through the state privatisation agency, the National Property Fund, the state controls 91.3 percent of Slovenska Sporitelna, 50.5 percent Slovenska Poistovna, some 35 percent in IRB and about 51.49 percent in VUB.
The original law suspending bank privatisation was approved last month after the ultra-left ZRS, a junior partner in the ruling coalition, voted with the opposition.
The government, however, then asked President Michal Kovac to return the law for re-assessment, which he promptly did.

The opposition approved the original law because it wanted the banks to be restructured before selling the state's stake, and feared many of the shares would end up in hands of Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's allies.
